sources.title: Human History Map: indexed Azerbaijan records and decoded borders
sources.note: Own-project factual-data exception. Local index and all relevant border features decoded in identity.json. Exact modern ID starts 1994, to null; unchanged historical multipolygons through 2020, different modern outline for 2020 to 2100. Both include mainland and Nakhchivan. No claim these show contemporaneous control or predict 2100.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Azerbaijan diplomatic history
sources.note: Direct official diplomatic history read. US recognition 25 December 1991, following Soviet dissolution; earlier independence ended in April 1920. Recognition date is not presented as independence declaration date.

sources.title: Constitution of Azerbaijan: official English text
sources.note: Direct current consolidated text, adopted 12 November 1995 and effective 27 November 1995, with later amendments. Articles 7, 42 and 45 checked. Constitutional descriptions are legal provisions, not independent evidence of implementation. This and Azerbaijani version count as one work in manual budget.

sources.title: Azərbaycan Respublikasının Konstitusiyası: official Azerbaijani text
sources.note: Direct Article 42.I, exact Hər bir vətəndaşın təhsil almaq hüququ vardır. Official English Article 42.I supplies translation. Current consolidated modern-type text, not a photograph of a 1995 original. Seven Azerbaijani plus eight English quoted words; combined constitutional work budget checked.

sources.title: OSCE/ODIHR: Azerbaijan presidential election of 15 October 2003, final report
sources.note: Original 32-page final report dated 12 November 2003 directly read. Executive summary and background, plus printed page 10 on Heydar Aliyev withdrawing in favor of his son Ilham. CEC declaration of winner reported as such; independent assessment does not certify a fair election.

sources.title: OSCE: lack of genuine political alternatives characterized Azerbaijan election
sources.note: Direct observer press release 8 February 2024 about 7 February vote. Efficient preparation but no genuine pluralism; restrictions, suppressed critical voices and serious count concerns. Assessment clearly attributed and dated.

sources.title: Associated Press: Armenia asks UN court to protect Nagorno-Karabakh Armenians
sources.note: Original AP indexed article read: 1994 Armenian-backed control, 2020 Azerbaijani territorial gains, 19 September 2023 offensive, internationally recognized Azerbaijani territory. Limited to historical background in one passage; AP attribution remains below the returned 100-word limit.

sources.title: UNHCR and partners: Armenia rapid needs assessment, October 2023
sources.note: Original PDF directly read, printed page 5 context: over 100,000 ethnic Armenians fled Nagorno-Karabakh for Armenia during last week of September 2023. Refugee impacts, not a claim about current regional population or border control.

sources.title: ICRC: Nagorno-Karabakh conflict operational update, December 2020
sources.note: Direct 15 December 2020 operational report. Damage to homes, schools and hospitals; missing persons and mine risks. Water and habitation section: 66 families in shelters received showers and latrines. These are regional figures covering the conflict response, not Azerbaijan-only figures.

sources.title: Joint US, Armenian and Azerbaijani statement on the peace summit anniversary
sources.note: Direct 10 August 2026 trilateral statement on Armenian MFA site. Paragraph 1 distinguishes signed 2025 Joint Declaration from initialed draft interstate agreement. First bullet reports border stability and continuing normalization/delimitation. Public wording attributes those claims and does not assert treaty ratification, final border settlement, completed transit routes or live control.

sources.title: Statoil, now Equinor: First Caspian oil lifted in the Mediterranean
sources.note: Direct project participant report dated 6 June 2006. British Hawthorn carried first BTC cargo from Ceyhan; route Baku via Georgia to Turkey. Contemporary corporate production targets not adopted as achieved facts.

sources.title: UNESCO: Baku removed from the World Heritage Danger List
sources.note: Direct 25 June 2009 report. Preservation improvements led to removal; earthquake damage in November 2000, urban development pressures and weak conservation had led to danger listing in 2003. Medieval monuments are inherited heritage, not modern constructions.

sources.title: UNESCO: Dolma making and sharing tradition
sources.note: Original full indexed UNESCO text read; direct page challenges automated access. Reproducible query UNESCO Dolma making sharing tradition 01188. 2017 inscription, ingredients and parent-child/vocational transmission; variation across communities explicit. No exclusive-origin claim.

sources.title: UNESCO: Traditional art of Azerbaijani carpet weaving
sources.note: Full indexed UNESCO text verified at institutional host f5vip11.unesco.org with identical path. Family teaching, winter weaving, knots and flat weave, solemn cutting from loom. Normal-host direct access challenged; no medical efficacy or universal household/gender claim.

sources.title: UNESCO: Culture of Çay, joint Azerbaijan and Türkiye inscription
sources.note: Indexed original decision and original listing 01685 read; direct access challenged. Joint 2022 inscription, hospitality and pear-shaped cups, accompaniments. Alternate indexed listing slug moutya-01685 resolves title Tea; public source uses stable decision number.

sources.title: UNICEF: For every child in Azerbaijan, what we achieved together
sources.note: Direct regional UNICEF article dated 2 September 2025. Preschool enrollment 14 percent in 2015 and 35 percent in 2024, home-visiting model and development/vaccination support. Future enrollment targets not presented as achieved. Article discusses country-office closure and regional transition; no current office claim.

sources.title: European Observatory and WHO: Health Systems in Action 2024, Azerbaijan
sources.note: Direct 4 December 2024 report summary. Mandatory insurance coverage, exclusions for most outpatient medicines/dental care; urban-rural shortages. Describes policy as of 2024 and distinguishes entitlement from access.

sources.title: WHO: Azerbaijan strengthens its health workforce to boost primary healthcare
sources.note: Direct 12 October 2021 report, Shamakhi project: three mobile clinics, trained staff, rural outreach. No inference that all rural districts had these clinics or that project continues unchanged today.

sources.title: World Bank: Bringing reliable water supply and sanitation to Azerbaijan
sources.note: Direct original results report. Eight selected districts, project results 2008 to 2019: 46,000 household water connections, 43,000 sewer connections. Beneficiary Sevinj Novruzova in Siyazan describes buckets and new taps. Page has inconsistent publication metadata, so public text dates project results, not publication. No national toilet-coverage percentage inferred.

proposedOverrides.name: Azerbaijan (modern republic)
proposedOverrides.summary: Modern Azerbaijan: independence, presidential government, conflict and diplomacy, family traditions, education, healthcare and changing household infrastructure.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct modern republic card, no association with earlier azerbaijan 1914 to 1938, Soviet republic, khanates or disputed neighboring records.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Three historical multipolygons repeat identical bounds from 1994 to 2020: [44.671046710467124,38.30932559593,50.46710467104671,41.88850771631922]. Mainland plus western Nakhchivan component. Modern 2020 to 2100 multipolygon has bounds [44.794,38.27,50.393,41.861], also two components. These atlas shapes do not establish contemporaneous administrative or military control. Raw decoded coordinates and component bounds are retained in identity.json.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Index 1994 to null is display coverage. Independence 1991 supplied as explicit background. Constitution 1995, succession 2003, war 2020, exodus 2023, election 2024, declaration 2025 and dated joint statement 10 August 2026 kept distinct. No final treaty ratification, final border or current control claim.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact current official Azerbaijani Article 42.I paired with official English translation, both directly read. Modern Latin text of consolidated 1995 constitution, not an archival facsimile. Constitution and translation grouped as one work for budget.
batchIdentityNotes.scope: ICRC shelter showers and latrines are a regional 2020 aid statistic, not Azerbaijan-only. Water project covers eight districts; health and school statistics carry dates. UNESCO food/craft practices are documented community traditions, not universal behaviors or exclusive origin claims.
batchIdentityNotes.access: Most institutions directly read. UNESCO ICH pages challenged automated opening; full indexed originals supply the specific passages with reproducible queries. AP historical background read in indexed original and kept below its stricter 100-word limit. Current political detail uses precisely attributed primary statements alongside independent election observations.
